svg.text: How backend_engine="FEM" plugs a frequency-domain finite-element solver (S-parameters + far field) into the existing openEMS pipeline.
1 · Backend switch through the shared pipeline
The user builds geometry exactly as for FDTD; four SimTools methods branch on sim.backend_engine.

g.text: → SimSetup(CSX, FDTD, freqs, backend, N, FemOptions)
geometry built into CSX (same as FDTD)

svg.text: FEM gain uses input_power = Prad + Ploss
2 · fem_backend orchestration — stages, file artifacts (in output_path), external tools
Each stage is stateless: state is handed to the next stage through files, not Python objects. The far field is solved on demand.
fem_backend orchestrates the pipeline; sim_tools lazily imports fem_backend + fem_radiation; fem_materials is the shared leaf (region-ID contract + constants).
Solid grey → import. Dashed purple → external tool.
sim_tools imports fem_backend / fem_radiation lazily inside
the FEM branches — FDTD users never load them.
fem_geometry & fem_formulation take Problem / Mesh type hints
from fem_backend, but only under TYPE_CHECKING — no runtime cycle.
S(f) of a linear structure is a smooth rational function, so a few full solves reconstruct the whole curve.
Loop: build model → pick_next → one FEM solve → re-fit, until the budget or tolerance is met.
Typically 8–15 solves reproduce a 200+ point sweep.
